chunks: [Project cover](https://www.figma.com/design/m0v1MINOJA152Kil6JHeZ8/Agentplace?node-id=130-1323) is a shared asset reference used by cards, picker thumbnails and the agent experience. Preserve the image crop; use a branded or empty fallback. Upload, replace and remove affect the draft first. Persist and publish separately.

For responsive code use a bottom field height clamp(360px, 44.444vw, 640px), blur clamp(160px, 20.833vw, 300px), and scale travel down with viewport width. Keep the field decorative and behind scrolling content; it must not cover controls, create horizontal scroll or become a fixed foreground overlay. Avoid one canvas per component, full-screen animated blur or per-frame layout measurements. The companion CSS example implements the same cycle using transformed gradient layers; a GPU shader is optional, not required.

OTP state machine: empty/partial → complete → verifying → verified or error. Six numeric digits are a string, including leading zeroes. Paste/autofill distributes all digits. Verify remains disabled until the code is complete; a second submit during verification has no effect. Keep entered digits on recoverable errors and move focus to the relevant correction point. Expiry or invalid-code messages must explain the next action and allow resend when eligible.

- Project: id, name, lifecycle, hasUnpublishedChanges, updatedAt, coverAssetId, publishedVersionId.
- Draft: projectId, versionId, agentConfig, branding, instructions, skillBindings.
- Generation job: id, projectId, status, currentStep, error, resumable.
- Published version: immutable versionId and public URL. Publishing changes the live pointer; editing a draft does not.

Keep company logo and agent avatar separate. A cover can be uploaded, replaced or removed and reused in cards and the agent experience. Validate file type and size, show upload progress/failure, preserve the previous image until replacement succeeds, and expose crop/alt-text handling where relevant.

Branding changes stage a draft and the preview can reflect local changes immediately. Save changes persists the draft. The saved state must reflect a successful response. Publishing is a separate action. Removing a cover restores the agreed fallback everywhere that draft asset is consumed.
Only example Added/Empty cover states are drawn. File picker, validation error, upload progress and crop details still need implementation and focused visual QA.

The Figma file documents desktop visuals and sample prototype flows. It does not implement backend authentication, persistence, clipboard, uploads, billing, invitations, plugin consent, responsive pages, OTP errors/expiry, generation errors/cancel, or permission-denied screens. Build these behaviors from the contracts above using the existing components, and review their error/empty/loading states before release. Do not infer a deployed API or complete runtime from a prototype link.

Maintain explicit async states: idle, validating, submitting/working, success and error. Disable duplicate submissions, preserve user input and recover from failed persistence. Network/server outcomes determine transitions; prototype timeouts must not become production logic.

Required evidence: six-digit paste and leading-zero OTP; blocked duplicate submit; loading widths stay stable; project switching retains the correct data; draft edits do not alter live content; role restrictions are enforced by the server; failed save/upload/publish can recover; menus/dialogs restore focus; reduced motion has no decorative movement.
